cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Confess Around Them
cards.instruction: Use partial admissions to make a reciprocal confession feel like the only missing piece.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I changed the meeting time. Did you change the room?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Yes. That's my half of why nobody met.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I should have. Now tell me where your half of the meeting went.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 admits changing time and asks B room; A3 rules that admission is A half; A5 briefly concedes nondisclosure then orders B missing half. Authority defines reciprocal confession as required.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2 surprise with partial admission; A5 answers B4 why-not-tell with concession before returning demand for B role.

relationship.evidence: B2 is surprised and B4 asks a fair communication question, a plausible participant in the failed meeting.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 nondisclosure question to add an admission that increases pressure for reciprocal room disclosure.

specificity.evidence: A1 changed meeting time/room and A3 nobody met establish practical failure; B room change remains a question, not fact.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 where your half went echoes actual missed location; prefixes remain redundant but operative half-accounting is clear.
